statutes.title: Statutes
statutes.description: Statutes of Skills Lab e.V. (English translation for information) with table of contents: name and seat, purpose, non-profit status, membership, fees, bodies, general meeting, board, dissolution.

sections.title: § 1 Name, registered office, financial year
paras: The association is called “Skills Lab”. It is to be entered in the register of associations and will then bear the suffix “e.V.”.
The association has its registered office in Erbach (Odenwald). [Placeholder]
The financial year is the calendar year.

sections.title: § 2 Purpose of the association
paras: The purpose of the association is the promotion of adult and vocational education.

This purpose is achieved in particular through courses, workshops, talks and open learning activities on communication, digital skills, presenting, self-organisation and languages, which are open to anyone interested.
The association is politically and religiously neutral.

sections.title: § 3 Non-profit status
paras: The association pursues exclusively and directly non-profit purposes within the meaning of the section “Tax-privileged purposes” of the German Fiscal Code (Abgabenordnung).
The association acts selflessly; it does not primarily pursue its own economic purposes.

sections.title: § 4 Use of funds
paras: The association’s funds may only be used for the purposes set out in these statutes. Members do not receive any payments from the association’s funds.
No person may benefit from expenses that are unrelated to the purpose of the association or from disproportionately high remuneration.

Board members and course leaders may receive appropriate compensation for their expenses within the limits of the budget (e.g. under section 3 no. 26 or no. 26a German Income Tax Act). The board decides on this.

sections.title: § 5 Membership
paras: Any natural person and any legal entity that supports the aims of the association may become a member.
The association has full members and supporting members. Supporting members support the association financially; they have no voting rights.
The board decides on written or electronic applications for membership. Minors require the consent of their legal guardians. A rejection does not need to be justified.

sections.title: § 6 End of membership
paras: Membership ends through resignation, expulsion, death or, for legal entities, their dissolution.
Resignation is made by declaration in text form to the board. It is possible with three months’ notice to the end of the financial year.

A member may be expelled by resolution of the board if they act in serious breach of the association’s interests or, despite two reminders, are more than one year in arrears with their fee. Before the resolution, the member must be given the opportunity to comment. The member may appeal against the expulsion to the general meeting within one month.

sections.title: § 7 Fees
paras: Members pay annual fees.
The amount, due date and method of payment are set out in membership fee rules adopted by the general meeting.
In justified cases, the board may defer, reduce or waive fees in whole or in part.

sections.title: § 8 Bodies of the association
paras: The bodies of the association are the general meeting and the board.

sections.title: § 9 General meeting
paras: The ordinary general meeting takes place once a year. An extraordinary general meeting must be convened if the interests of the association require it or if one tenth of the members entitled to vote request it in text form, stating the reasons.

The board convenes the general meeting in text form (e.g. by email) with three weeks’ notice, stating the agenda. It may also take place virtually or in hybrid form; the board decides this in the invitation.

The general meeting is responsible in particular for: electing and discharging the board, electing the auditors, receiving the annual report, adopting the membership fee rules, amending the statutes and dissolving the association.
Every full member aged 16 or over has one vote. A duly convened general meeting has a quorum regardless of the number of members present.
Resolutions are passed by a simple majority of valid votes cast unless these statutes provide otherwise. Abstentions are not counted.
Minutes of the resolutions are taken and signed by the chair of the meeting and the person taking the minutes.

sections.title: § 10 Board
paras: The board consists of the chair, the vice chair and the treasurer.
The association is represented in and out of court by two board members jointly (board within the meaning of section 26 German Civil Code).
The board is elected by the general meeting for two years. It remains in office until a new board is elected.
The board manages the affairs of the association unless the general meeting is responsible. It may adopt rules of procedure and delegate tasks to members or working groups.

sections.title: § 11 Audit
paras: The general meeting elects two auditors for two years who are not members of the board.
They audit the accounts once a year and report to the general meeting.

sections.title: § 12 Data protection
paras: The association processes personal data of its members, participants and donors exclusively to fulfil its statutory tasks and in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the German Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG).
The board may lay down further details in data protection rules.

sections.title: § 13 Amendments to the statutes
paras: Amendments to the statutes require a two-thirds majority of the valid votes cast. They can only be adopted if they were announced in the invitation to the general meeting.
The board alone may make amendments that the register court or the tax office require for formal reasons. It informs the members about this.

sections.title: § 14 Dissolution and allocation of assets
paras: The dissolution of the association can only be decided at a general meeting convened specifically for this purpose, by a three-quarters majority of the valid votes cast.

If the association is dissolved or its tax-privileged purposes cease to apply, its assets pass to [name of a legal entity under public law or another tax-privileged body], which must use them directly and exclusively for non-profit purposes, namely the promotion of adult and vocational education.
These statutes come into force upon entry in the register of associations.

fees.title: Membership fee rules
fees.description: Membership fee rules of Skills Lab e.V. (English translation for information): fees for individual, reduced, family, supporting and corporate members, due date, payment, joining and leaving.
fees.h1: Membership fee rules of Skills Lab e.V.
fees.intro: These membership fee rules are based on § 7 of the statutes. They do not form part of the statutes.
fees.amounts_placeholder: All amounts are placeholders to be set by the general meeting.

sections.title: § 1 Amount of fees
paras: The association charges annual fees as shown in the following table.
For supporting and corporate members, the amount shown is a minimum fee. A higher fee is welcome.

sections.title: § 2 Due date
paras: The annual fee is due on 31 January of each year for the current financial year.
When joining during the year, the fee is due one month after admission.

sections.title: § 3 Method of payment
paras: The fee is preferably collected by SEPA direct debit. For this, the member grants a SEPA direct debit mandate. The association announces the collection at least five days in advance (pre-notification).
Alternatively, the fee may be transferred to the association’s account. Please state your name and “Membership fee [year]” as the payment reference.
Costs of returned direct debits for which the member is responsible (e.g. insufficient funds, changed bank details) are borne by the member.

sections.title: § 4 Joining during the year
paras: Members joining in the first half of the year pay the full annual fee; members joining from 1 July pay half the annual fee.

sections.title: § 5 Leaving
paras: Resignation is governed by § 6 of the statutes (three months’ notice to the end of the financial year).
Fees already paid are not refunded on resignation or expulsion.

sections.title: § 6 Reductions and exemptions
paras: The reduced fee applies to school pupils, apprentices, students, pensioners and recipients of social benefits. Proof must be submitted to the board every year without being asked.
In cases of particular hardship, the board may, on application, defer, further reduce or waive the fee. Applications are treated confidentially.

sections.title: § 7 Late payment
paras: If a fee has not been paid two months after it falls due, the association sends a reminder in text form. After a second unsuccessful reminder, the board may expel the member in accordance with § 6 of the statutes.
No reminder fees are charged. [Placeholder – to be decided by the association]

sections.title: § 8 Entry into force
paras: These membership fee rules come into force by resolution of the general meeting on {site:documents.fees_date}.

The controller responsible for data processing on this website is:

sections.title: 2. Summary
paras: This website does not use cookies or tracking and does not load fonts or scripts from third-party servers. We only process personal data if you provide it yourself via a form or by email, and in the technically necessary server log files. The map on the contact page is only loaded with your consent.

sections.title: 3. Hosting and server log files
paras: The website is hosted by [name and address of the hosting provider]. A data processing agreement has been concluded with the host (Art. 28 GDPR). [Placeholder]

When you access the pages, the server automatically stores: IP address, date and time, page requested, amount of data transferred, browser and operating system, and the previously visited page. This is necessary for secure operation. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in a stable and secure website). Log files are deleted after [7] days. [Placeholder – ask the host]

sections.title: 4. Local storage in your browser
paras: We only store the following in your browser (localStorage): your chosen language, your chosen appearance (light/dark) and your decision about the map. This information does not leave your device. The legal basis is section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG (strictly necessary or expressly requested by you). You can delete this information at any time via your browser settings.

sections.title: 5. Contact form and email
paras: If you write to us via the contact form or by email, we process your name, email address, topic and message in order to answer your enquiry. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (enquiries about courses and membership) or Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (other enquiries). We delete the data once the enquiry has been dealt with, at the latest after [12] months, unless statutory retention obligations apply.

sections.title: 6. Newsletter
paras: For the newsletter, we need your email address and your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). We use the double opt-in procedure: you receive an email with a confirmation link and are only added after confirming. We store the time of subscription and confirmation as proof. You can unsubscribe at any time via the link in every newsletter or by email; we will then delete your address from the mailing list.
We use [name of the newsletter service] for sending. A data processing agreement has been concluded with the service. [Placeholder]

sections.title: 7. Membership applications and membership administration
paras: For membership, we process: name, address, email address, phone number if provided, date of birth, type of membership, date of joining, method of payment and fee payments. We need the date of birth to check the type of membership and voting rights. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (membership relationship under the statutes).

Only board members have access, to the extent they need the data for their tasks. After membership ends, we delete the data unless it must be retained due to tax retention obligations (including section 147 German Fiscal Code).

sections.title: 8. SEPA direct debit
paras: If you grant a SEPA direct debit mandate, we process the account holder, IBAN and mandate reference to collect fees. The data is transmitted to our bank [name of bank] to execute the direct debit. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR. We retain the mandate in accordance with legal requirements.
The IBAN check in the form only takes place in your browser; no data is transmitted.

sections.title: 9. Donations and donation receipts
paras: For a donation or donation request, we process your name, email address, amount, frequency, address and message if provided, and the details from your bank transfer, in order to record the donation, thank you and, on request, issue a donation receipt. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) and (c) GDPR.

We retain donation records and copies of donation receipts in accordance with tax regulations (including section 147 German Fiscal Code, section 50 German Income Tax Implementing Ordinance) – for up to ten years depending on the document. [Periods to be checked by the association or a tax adviser]
The GiroCode on the donation page is generated entirely in your browser. No data is transmitted to us or to third parties.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.description: Accessibility statement for the Skills Lab e.V. website: status of WCAG 2.2 AA implementation, known limitations and contact for feedback.

sections.title: Our aim
paras: Skills Lab e.V. wants everyone to be able to use this website. We have therefore designed it in line with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, level AA. We publish this statement voluntarily.

sections.title: Compliance status
paras: Based on our own assessment, the website is largely compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA. Checks included: keyboard-only use, visible focus, colour contrast, heading structure, form labels, error messages, display at 320 px width and when zoomed, and automated testing with axe-core. A review by external experts or by people with disabilities is still pending. [Assessment date: {site:build_date}]

sections.title: What we have implemented
paras: “Skip to content” link · clear headings and regions · all functions usable with a keyboard · high contrast in light and dark mode · forms with labels, hints and clear error messages · tables with column headers · no motion when “reduce motion” is enabled · text alternative for the GiroCode · content in three languages.

sections.title: Known limitations
paras: Map: The OpenStreetMap map is external content and not fully accessible. The address is therefore always shown as text on the page as well.

PDF documents: The statutes, membership fee rules and donation receipt template are generated from the web pages and are only available in German. Their accessibility has not been fully checked. All content is also available as web pages.
GiroCode: The code itself can only be used visually. All the data it contains is shown next to it as text and can be copied.
Translations: The English and Russian versions have not yet been reviewed by native speakers.

sections.title: Report a barrier
